mutant:features/duplicates.feature#Match.reason: Three mechanisms across ten mutants, recorded under one reason because approval is scoped per scenario and not per mutant - and because approve stamps every survivor in the scenario, not only the ones the gate reports as unapproved. Read this as three records. (a) Rows already excluded on a single dimension - the policy-mismatch row and the loss-type-mismatch row - yield no match whatever the mutated column holds, so mutating any other dimension on them is inert. Four mutants. (b) Rows excluded by loss-date distance: their policy number and their loss type both agree with the existing claim, so neither is what excludes them, and substituting either leaves the outcome unchanged. Four mutants. (c) Matching rows whose loss date is swapped for another in-window date: the substituted date is also inside the window, so the match survives - a swap to an out-of-window date flips the result and is killed, which means the boundary is proven by the in-window and out-of-window rows jointly and never by a single row. Two mutants. Rows are described by role rather than by literal value, per the convention in docs/harness-findings.md: example data is what a vocabulary pass changes, so a reason quoting it decays while its locator stays valid. REVISIT TRIGGER: void if the window changes from 60 days, if policy or loss-type equality stops being part of the match key, or if this Examples table gains a second row whose policy number matches the existing claim.

REVISIT TRIGGER: void if either scenario's example dates are changed such that an interval lands within one day of its threshold.

mutant:features/triage.feature#From raw.reason:
All eleven survivors in this scenario are equivalent. They share one record because `gauntlet mutant approve` stamps every survivor in the scenario with one reason and all eleven fall here; --scenario cannot isolate a subset. Written 2026-08-15, sized to all eleven.

EIGHT are loss-amount mutations. Severity derives from loss type alone and nothing in the domain reads the amount, so no mutation of that column can change severity, queue, or either indicator. The column is retained deliberately to demonstrate that independence (ASSUMPTIONS.md, item 4c); these eight survivors are the demonstration.

TWO are coverage-start mutations on rows whose substituted date sits 78 days before that row's loss date against a 30-day threshold - outside the window before and after, so the indicator resolves FALSE either way.

THE ELEVENTH is a separate judgment and this paragraph is its own record: the coverage-start mutation on the theft row that fires late reporting and carries a coverage-start value. The substituted date postdates that row's loss date, producing a negative interval that resolves FALSE only because a coverage start later than the loss date is rejected before the threshold is applied (`_evaluate_recent_inception`, src/claimgate/domain/siu.py; symbol name verified 2026-08-15 - the text this replaces named `_is_recent_inception`, which has not existed since 2026-08-09). That behaviour IS specified: siu_indicators.feature's Rule on a continuous coverage date after the loss date covers it, and tests/unit/test_siu.py exercises it. The mutant is unkillable HERE not because the specification is silent but because this scenario asserts routing invariance, not indicator boundaries. It is structurally unavoidable rather than a data-choice artifact: the scenario must exercise recent inception TRUE and late reporting TRUE, which together guarantee that some coverage-start value in the column postdates some loss date in the column.

REVISIT TRIGGER, applying only to the eleventh mutant: this approval is void if the rejection of a coverage-start date later than the loss date is removed, relaxed, or replaced - regardless of what the function implementing it is named at the time. Removal would also fail siu_indicators.feature's guard Rule and tests/unit/test_siu.py, both true as of 2026-08-15.

Read this as two records. (a) Narrowing cannot rescue a rejection. Two mutants, one in each column. (b) Widening cannot break an acceptance. On the row whose prefix sits inside the configured set, adding a further prefix leaves the original one recognized, so the notice is still accepted. One mutant. What does kill, and what these rows exist for, is the pair that moves one policy number across the set boundary: the same number rejected under the narrow set and accepted under the widened one. That boundary is proven by the pair jointly and never by a single row, so none of these three survivors weakens it. Shape violations - digit count, case, separator - live in their own outline where the configured set is fixed above the table and therefore inert; nothing there survives, which is the check that this rule and the shape rule stayed separate. Rows are described by role rather than by literal value, per the convention in docs/harness-findings.md: example data is what a vocabulary pass changes, so a reason quoting it decays while its locator stays valid. REVISIT TRIGGER: void if an unrecognized prefix stops resolving POLICY_NUMBER_MALFORMED and gains a reason code of its own, if the number shape becomes configurable, or if this outline gains a row whose policy number is accepted under every configured set it appears with.

mutant:features/validation.feature#Requi.reason: Twelve mutants across two mechanisms, recorded under one reason because approval is scoped per scenario and not per mutant - and because approve stamps every survivor in the scenario, not only the ones the gate reports as unapproved. Read this as two records. (a) A configuration flag mutated on a row where the field that flag guards is populated: the required-field check is reachable only when the field is absent, so on those rows the flag is never consulted and flipping it cannot change any blocker. Eight mutants, four per flag. (b) A field value mutated on a row where that field's own flag reads not-required: nothing reads the value on those rows, so substituting or blanking it is inert. Four mutants, two per field. Neither mechanism weakens the outline. Each flag is proven to be consulted by the pair of rows where its field is absent, one row per flag state, and that pair is what kills the flag mutation, because the outcome differs across it - the boundary is proven by the pair jointly and never by a single row. The unconditional field is proven by the row where both flags read not-required and it alone blocks; no mutation of either flag can rescue that row, which is why nothing survives in the description or blockers columns. This outline has a parallel twin for the other Section II loss type, identical by design (QUEUE.md item 4g) - that symmetry is why loss type is not a column here and why the same reason applies to both. Rows are described by role rather than by literal value, per the convention in docs/harness-findings.md: example data is what a vocabulary pass changes, so a reason quoting it decays while its locator stays valid. REVISIT TRIGGER: void if incident_description becomes configurable, if a claimant field is added or removed, if either flag comes to gate more than one field, or if the two Section II outlines ever stop being identical to one another.
